The three numbers that decide a challenge

Every prop firm evaluation comes down to a profit target and two loss limits. The profit target (commonly 8-10%) is what everybody watches, and it is rarely what ends a run. The maximum drawdown is your overall floor: static floors sit at the starting balance minus the limit and never move, while trailing floors follow your highest equity upward, so profit you give back counts against you. The daily loss limit is the one that does the damage. It resets every day from that day's opening equity, it ignores how far ahead you are, and on most firms it counts open losses too - one session sized to win back a loss is enough.

That is why sizing has to start from the tightest limit, not from the target. If a single stop loss costs half your daily room, two losers in a row end the day and a third ends the account. Put your own numbers in above: the calculator shows the floor that binds right now, how many full-size losers in a row you can absorb before breaking it, and the position size that keeps one stop inside your chosen risk.

Crypto challenges have one more wrinkle. The market never closes, so "the day" is a clock, usually 00:00 UTC, and a position held across it carries its open loss into tomorrow's starting equity. Know your firm's reset time before you hold anything overnight.

FAQ

What is trailing drawdown on a prop firm account?
Trailing drawdown is a loss limit measured from the highest equity your account has reached, not from where it started. On a $10,000 account with a 6% trailing drawdown the floor starts at $9,400; if you grow the account to $10,800 the floor moves up to $10,152. It never moves down, so profit you give back counts against you. Some firms stop the trail once it reaches the starting balance.
What is the difference between static and trailing drawdown?
A static drawdown floor is fixed at the starting balance minus the limit and never moves. A trailing floor follows your peak equity upward. Static is more forgiving: once you are in profit you have more room than you started with. Trailing means a winning streak raises the bar you must stay above.
How is the daily loss limit calculated?
Most firms take the balance (or equity) at the start of the trading day and subtract the daily percentage of the starting account size. On crypto challenges the day usually resets at 00:00 UTC, because the market never closes - check your firm, some use their server time. Open losses usually count, so a position sitting in a drawdown can break the rule before you close it.
Does unrealised loss count toward the drawdown?
At most firms yes: the limit is checked against equity, which includes the open profit and loss of positions you are still holding. That is why a stop loss matters more on a challenge than anywhere else - a trade you intend to hold through a dip can end the account while it is still open.
How much should I risk per trade on a prop firm challenge?
Size from the tightest limit, which is almost always the daily loss. A common rule is that one full stop loss should never cost more than a third to a half of the daily limit, so two losers in a row still leave you trading tomorrow. On a 4% daily limit that is roughly 1-2% of the account per trade. The calculator above does that arithmetic for your stop distance.
Which rule fails the most prop firm challenges?
Measured on our own traders, the daily loss limit ends far more runs than the overall drawdown, and the profit target is rarely the problem. It resets every day and ignores how far ahead you were, so one bad session sized to win back a loss is enough. The live count is on this page and at /api/funded.
